name: Synthetic dreads

card.summary: Artificial dreadlock extensions made from synthetic fibre that are attached to natural hair to add length, volume or colour without committing to real locs.
card.aka: dread extensions, dread falls, cyberlox, cyberlocks
card.note: Temporary; wear time runs from weeks to months depending on installation and care.

quick.overview:
Synthetic dreads are rope-like locs made from synthetic fibre such as Kanekalon. They are attached to natural hair by braiding or crocheting, or worn as falls, to get the look of dreadlocks, including bright colours and long lengths, without growing real locs.

The appearance payoff is a fast, reversible change of hairstyle, plus added length and volume. Information comes mainly from commercial and encyclopedic descriptions; no clinical studies are listed.
quick.how: They are installed in a salon or at home by braiding or crocheting the synthetic locs into the natural hair, in single-ended or double-ended forms. They are taken out when the wearer wants and can often be reused.
quick.risks: Heavy installations can tug on the scalp and natural hair, and the fibre is a non-biodegradable plastic. Grokipedia describes them as lighter and less tension-causing than permanent installations, but individual experience varies.

lead: Synthetic dreads are artificial dreadlock extensions made from synthetic fibres such as Kanekalon and attached to natural hair by braiding or crocheting. [1] They give the look of dreadlocks, in colours and lengths natural hair does not easily provide, without the permanent change of real locs. [1]

Grokipedia traces them to the 1990s cybergoth scene, where neon 'cyberlox' became a fashion statement, and describes festival and cosplay use as well as protective-style use. [1] Because the descriptions here come from a single AI-generated encyclopedia entry, details should be read as indicative.

chain: Synthetic locs braided or crocheted into hair
Dreadlock look without growing real locs
angle.text: They change hair appearance immediately and reversibly, adding colour, length and the dreadlock silhouette. They can be removed when the wearer chooses.

paras: Synthetic dreads consist of bundled synthetic fibre twisted, backcombed or crocheted into rope-like strands. Single-ended pieces blend into the hair at one end, while double-ended pieces are folded for fuller coverage. [1]
Fibres named include Kanekalon, Toyokalon and jumbo braid hair; Grokipedia reports they are colourfast and heat-resistant to roughly 160 degrees Celsius. [1]
Per Grokipedia, they emerged in the late 1990s among cybergoth and rave scenes, and online retailers began selling pre-made dread falls around 2009. [1]
The same source notes the fibre is petroleum-derived and non-biodegradable. [1]

timeline.event: Cyberlox emerge in the cybergoth scene (per Grokipedia). [1]
Specialised online retailers begin selling dread falls (per Grokipedia). [1]
